An inline liquid metering valve delivers a repeatable measured volume of concentrate into a flowing carrier liquid and rinses the surfaces that contacted the concentrate after each dose, without any command additional to the stroke that delivers the dose.

The valve has a housing with an inlet and an outlet and a metering sleeve fixed within the housing. The metering sleeve defines a dose chamber, a concentrate port opening into the dose chamber, a carrier-liquid admission port opening into the dose chamber, and a flush bypass that opens downstream of the dose chamber. A piston slides axially in the dose chamber between a fill position and a discharge position. The piston has an upstream sealing land and a downstream sealing land axially spaced from one another and joined by a reduced-diameter waist.

Separation of the two liquids is enforced by the axial order of the land faces and the port edges rather than by the sequence in which any external command arrives. In the fill position, the waist connects the concentrate port to the dose chamber while the upstream and downstream sealing lands isolate the carrier-liquid admission port from the concentrate port. Movement of the piston toward the discharge position closes the concentrate port before the downstream sealing land uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port. Carrier liquid then enters behind the measured volume of concentrate and expels that volume through a one-way outlet valve toward the outlet. Because one land face has passed the concentrate port before the other land face releases the carrier-liquid admission port, no position of the piston places the concentrate source in communication with the carrier-liquid path.

The rinse is carried out by the return of the same piston. An annular rinse channel lies between an outer surface of the metering sleeve and an inner surface of the housing, and at least one rinse opening leads from that channel through the metering sleeve into the dose chamber. A follower pin carried by the piston rod opens a normally closed flush poppet connected to the flush bypass during the return stroke, so that carrier liquid sweeps the annular rinse channel, issues from the rinse opening across the surfaces wetted by the concentrate, and leaves through the flush bypass to the outlet. The flush poppet closes before the waist reconnects the concentrate port to the dose chamber, so the rinse is complete, and the rinse liquid is on its way to the outlet, before any further concentrate can enter. The rinse cannot be omitted, mistimed or deferred, because the element that opens it is carried by the piston rod itself.

In described embodiments, a flexible lip on the upstream sealing land wipes the wall of the dose chamber before the flush poppet opens. Two radial rinse openings are directed across the concentrate port and across the one-way outlet valve.

Dose selection is mechanical and self-indexing. An index collar surrounds the metering sleeve and has a helical cam groove engaged by the follower pin, so that each full stroke of the piston turns the index collar by one increment. Three selectable axial stop faces on the index collar limit the travel of the piston and thereby set three dose volumes, a spring-biased detent engaging one of three recesses retains the selected setting, and a transparent window in the housing shows one of three dose setting numerals carried by the index collar, so that the setting is visible without electronics.

A replaceable cartridge contains the piston, the metering sleeve, the one-way outlet valve and the flush poppet, and is retained by a threaded end cap. Removing the threaded end cap withdraws the cartridge without disturbing the connections at the inlet and the outlet.

A corresponding method admits concentrate to the dose chamber, closes the concentrate port before uncovering the carrier-liquid admission port, expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve, and then opens the flush poppet with the follower pin during the return of the piston and closes it again before the concentrate port is reconnected.

In the following description, the terms upstream and downstream refer to the direction of travel of the carrier liquid from the inlet toward the outlet, and the terms axial and radial refer to the axis along which the piston slides.

FIG. 1 shows an inline liquid metering valve 10 having a cylindrical housing 12 with an inlet 14 at one axial end and an outlet 16 at the opposite axial end, a metering sleeve 18 fixed within the housing 12, a cartridge 64 retained in the housing 12 by a threaded end cap 66, and a transparent window 52 in the housing 12.

The inline liquid metering valve 10 is connected in a line that already carries a flowing carrier liquid. Carrier liquid enters at the inlet 14, passes along the housing 12, and leaves at the outlet 16. That flow is the main flow into which each dose of concentrate is delivered, and it is also the flow that rinses the valve. The metering sleeve 18 is spaced radially inward from the inner surface of the housing 12 over part of its length.

FIG. 2 shows the metering sleeve 18 defining a dose chamber 20, a concentrate port 22 opening into the dose chamber 20 and a carrier-liquid admission port 24 opening into the dose chamber 20. FIG. 2 further shows an upstream sealing land 30 and a downstream sealing land 32 joined by a reduced-diameter waist 34 in the fill position, and a one-way outlet valve 38.

The dose chamber 20 is cylindrical. The concentrate port 22 is a radial port through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and is connected in use to a concentrate source. The carrier-liquid admission port 24 passes through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 at an axial position downstream of the concentrate port 22, and admits carrier liquid to the dose chamber 20. The metering sleeve 18 further defines a flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20.

A piston 28 is axially slidable in the dose chamber 20 between a fill position and a discharge position. The upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 are axially spaced from one another on the piston 28 and are joined by the reduced-diameter waist 34. Each sealing land bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20, while the waist 34 stands clear of that wall. A piston rod 36 extends from the piston 28 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 and is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke. The one-way outlet valve 38 is arranged to pass liquid from the dose chamber 20 toward the outlet 16 and to prevent flow in the opposite direction.

In the fill position the waist 34 connects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20, and the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolate the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. Concentrate accordingly passes from the concentrate source through the concentrate port 22 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume of concentrate, the extent of which is fixed by the travel then permitted to the piston 28. Throughout the fill position the carrier-liquid path is closed to the concentrate, because the downstream sealing land 32 overlies the carrier-liquid admission port 24 while the upstream sealing land 30 closes the dose chamber 20 on the other side of the waist 34.

Movement of the piston 28 toward the discharge position closes the concentrate port 22 before the downstream sealing land 32 uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port 24. The upstream sealing land 30 arrives at the concentrate port 22 and shuts it while the downstream sealing land 32 is still overlying the carrier-liquid admission port 24. Only after that has happened does continued travel of the piston 28 carry the downstream sealing land 32 clear of the carrier-liquid admission port 24. Carrier liquid then enters through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume of concentrate in the dose chamber 20 and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16, where it joins the main flow.

The axial ordering of the faces of the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 relative to the edges of the concentrate port 22 and the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is chosen so that the concentrate port 22 is closed at every position of the piston 28 at which the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is open. There is accordingly no position of the piston 28 at which the concentrate source communicates directly with the carrier-liquid path. The separation of the two liquids is a property of the geometry of the piston 28 and the metering sleeve 18. It does not depend on the order in which external commands are given, on any control signal, or on the correct operation of a separately actuated shut-off element. A slow stroke, an interrupted stroke, or a stroke reversed part way through cannot open both ports at once, because the port that must close does so at an earlier point on the same continuous path of travel than the point at which the other port opens.

FIG. 3 shows the piston 28 during the return stroke toward the fill position, with a flexible lip 56, the follower pin 44 holding a flush poppet 58 open, an annular rinse channel 60, two radial rinse openings 62 of which one is directed across the concentrate port 22, and the flush bypass 26.

The flexible lip 56 is carried on the upstream sealing land 30 and bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20. As the return stroke begins, the flexible lip 56 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20.

The annular rinse channel 60 lies between an outer surface of the metering sleeve 18 and an inner surface of the housing 12, and is supplied with carrier liquid from the inlet 14. The two radial rinse openings 62 pass through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and connect the annular rinse channel 60 to the dose chamber 20. One of the two radial rinse openings 62 is directed across the concentrate port 22 and the other is directed across the one-way outlet valve 38.

The flush poppet 58 is normally closed and is connected to the flush bypass 26. Near the end of the return stroke, the follower pin 44 reaches the flush poppet 58 and opens it. Carrier liquid then flows from the inlet 14 through the annular rinse channel 60, through the two radial rinse openings 62 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 to the outlet 16. The rinse liquid therefore reaches the outlet 16, as the dose does, and is carried away in the main flow.

The flush poppet 58 closes before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. The concentrate port 22 is closed throughout the interval in which the annular rinse channel 60 communicates with the flush bypass 26. Only when the flush poppet 58 has closed does the continuing return of the piston 28 bring the waist 34 back into register with the concentrate port 22, at which point the dose chamber 20 is charged again for the next dose.

Because the follower pin 44 that opens the flush poppet 58 is carried by the piston rod 36, the rinse occurs once for every dose and at the same point in every cycle. It is not a separate operation, it needs no command, and it cannot be omitted while the valve continues to be used. The rinse also occurs while the concentrate port 22 is shut and after the wall of the dose chamber 20 has been wiped.

FIG. 4 shows an index collar 40 having a helical cam groove 42 engaged by a follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36, three selectable axial stop faces 46, a spring-biased detent 48 engaging one of three detent recesses 50, and three dose setting numerals 54.

The index collar 40 surrounds the metering sleeve 18. Each full stroke of the piston 28 draws the follower pin 44 along the helical cam groove 42 and turns the index collar 40 by one increment, so that the index collar 40 advances by itself as the valve is used and needs no separate indexing drive.

The three axial stop faces 46 are carried by the index collar 40 at different axial positions. The stop face presented by the current increment of rotation limits the travel of the piston 28 and thereby sets the dose volume, so that the three axial stop faces 46 correspond to three dose volumes. The spring-biased detent 48 engages one of the three detent recesses 50 to retain the selected setting until the index collar 40 is next indexed.

The transparent window 52 in the housing 12 shows one of the three dose setting numerals 54 carried by the index collar 40. The dose setting numeral presented at the transparent window 52 is the one associated with the axial stop face then limiting the travel of the piston 28, so that the dose setting is mechanically visible without electronics. What is seen at the transparent window 52 is the position of the index collar 40 itself.

The cartridge 64 contains the piston 28, the metering sleeve 18, the one-way outlet valve 38 and the flush poppet 58, and is removable from the housing 12 as a unit. Removing the threaded end cap 66 withdraws the cartridge 64 from the housing 12 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 without disturbing the connections at the inlet 14 and the outlet 16, so that the cartridge 64 is replaced as a unit while the housing 12 remains in the line.

In use, carrier liquid flows through the housing 12 from the inlet 14 to the outlet 16. With the piston 28 in the fill position, concentrate is admitted through the concentrate port 22 and past the waist 34 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume, the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolating the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. The piston 28 is then advanced toward the discharge position so as to close the concentrate port 22 and thereafter to uncover the carrier-liquid admission port 24 with the downstream sealing land 32. Carrier liquid is admitted through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16. The extent of the travel available to the piston 28, and therefore the measured volume, is fixed by the selected one of the three axial stop faces 46.

The piston 28 is then returned toward the fill position. During the return, the flexible lip 56 on the upstream sealing land 30 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20, and the follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36 opens the normally closed flush poppet 58. Carrier liquid flows through the annular rinse channel 60 between the metering sleeve 18 and the housing 12, through the two radial rinse openings 62 in the metering sleeve 18 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20 to the outlet 16. The flush poppet 58 is closed before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. Over the same full stroke, the follower pin 44 travelling in the helical cam groove 42 turns the index collar 40 by one increment, the spring-biased detent 48 enters the next of the three detent recesses 50, and the dose setting numeral then presented at the transparent window 52 shows the setting that will govern the next dose. The valve is thereby left charged, rinsed and set, ready for the following cycle.

The foregoing description sets out embodiments of the invention. A skilled reader may make changes of detail to the described embodiments without departing from the scope of the claims that follow.

The stop face presented by the current increment of rotation limits the travel of the piston 28 and thereby sets the dose volume, so that the three axial stop faces 46 correspond to three dose volumes. The spring-biased detent 48 engages one of the three detent recesses 50 to retain the selected setting until the index collar 40 is next indexed.

The transparent window 52 in the housing 12 shows one of the three dose setting numerals 54 carried by the index collar 40. The dose setting numeral presented at the transparent window 52 is the one associated with the axial stop face then limiting the travel of the piston 28, so that the dose setting is mechanically visible without electronics. What is seen at the transparent window 52 is the position of the index collar 40 itself.

The cartridge 64 contains the piston 28, the metering sleeve 18, the one-way outlet valve 38 and the flush poppet 58, and is removable from the housing 12 as a unit. Removing the threaded end cap 66 withdraws the cartridge 64 from the housing 12 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 without disturbing the connections at the inlet 14 and the outlet 16, so that the cartridge 64 is replaced as a unit while the housing 12 remains in the line.

In use, carrier liquid flows through the housing 12 from the inlet 14 to the outlet 16. With the piston 28 in the fill position, concentrate is admitted through the concentrate port 22 and past the waist 34 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume, the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolating the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. The piston 28 is then advanced toward the discharge position so as to close the concentrate port 22 and thereafter to uncover the carrier-liquid admission port 24 with the downstream sealing land 32. Carrier liquid is admitted through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16. The extent of the travel available to the piston 28, and therefore the measured volume, is fixed by the selected one of the three axial stop faces 46.

The piston 28 is then returned toward the fill position. During the return, the flexible lip 56 on the upstream sealing land 30 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20, and the follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36 opens the normally closed flush poppet 58. Carrier liquid flows through the annular rinse channel 60 between the metering sleeve 18 and the housing 12, through the two radial rinse openings 62 in the metering sleeve 18 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20 to the outlet 16. Over the same full stroke, the follower pin 44 travelling in the helical cam groove 42 turns the index collar 40 by one increment, the spring-biased detent 48 enters the next of the three detent recesses 50, and the dose setting numeral then presented at the transparent window 52 shows the setting that will govern the next dose. input.summary: The application body was already complete and, per the reviewer's own source ledger, fully traced to the inventor text, so I changed nothing in the title, field, background, summary, claims, abstract or numeral table. I corrected the three internal-consistency defects the reviewer identified, plus one cross-figure consequence of the second fix. (1) FIG. 4 no longer places the metering sleeve's left end outside the index collar: the collar now extends leftward past that end, with the sleeve's hidden outline in broken line, so the follower pin 44 sits at the same axial station in FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 and can be simultaneously engaged in the cam groove and bearing on the poppet stem. I also extended the poppet stem in FIG. 3 leftward past the sleeve's left end so it actually reaches the pin. (2) In FIG. 3 the left radial rinse opening 62 moved off the station covered by the upstream sealing land to a station just downstream of the piston, clear of both lands and aimed up and left toward the concentrate port, so the depicted rinse jet has an open path onward to the flush bypass. Because that same opening appears unnumbered in FIG. 2, I moved it there too, from beneath the concentrate port to right of the downstream sealing land, so the two sections do not put one opening at two axial stations. (3) The FIG. 3 paragraph of the detailed description now introduces "a follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36" with an indefinite article, and the FIG. 4 paragraph refers back to "the follower pin 44". One note on the record: the brief states that no prior-art search was run, and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the art available to this draft may be incomplete and the Background contains no citations. No claim scope, no numeral, and no disclosed structure was altered.
reasoning: Claim 1 carries two features that do real technical work and that the specification explains as solving stated problems: the axial ordering by which the concentrate port is shut before the downstream land uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port, so separation is a property of the moving geometry rather than of command sequencing; and the flush poppet opened by the follower pin on the piston rod during the return stroke, closing before the waist reconnects the concentrate port, so the rinse is an unavoidable part of the same stroke. With no reference listed in prior_art/INDEX.md, those are the features an argument would be built from, and both are stated in the specification in the same words as in the claim.

Left out of claim 1 deliberately: the index collar, the cam groove, the three stop faces, the detent, the window and the numerals, the flexible lip, the two-opening rinse arrangement, the cartridge and end cap, and the cylindrical housing with end-to-end ports. Each is a real fallback and each sits in a dependent claim (2, 3, 6 to 12), so claim 1 keeps only the ordered isolation and the stroke-driven rinse, which is the narrowest set that still makes the invention work.

The rinse channel and at least one rinse opening stay in claim 1 because the flush path recited in the last wherein clause needs antecedent structure to flow through; the count of rinse openings and their aiming is left to claim 2 so claim 1 is not limited to two.

Claims 4, 5 and 16 restate the disclosed ordering and the closed-port interval as separate positive limitations, so that if the wherein clauses of claim 1 are read as functional there is an express structural or timing fallback to retreat to.
The method claims 13 to 20 mirror the apparatus ladder because a valve maker and a valve user are different infringers, and the disclosure expressly asked for both classes.

On the drawings: the reviewer's finding that FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 put pin 44 on opposite sides of the sleeve's left end was correct, and the cure had to be on the FIG. 4 side, because FIG. 3's pin position is fixed by its need to reach the poppet stem. Extending the collar leftward over the sleeve end is a depiction arrangement only; it was not added to the description or the claims, and the description still says only that the index collar surrounds the metering sleeve.

On the left rinse opening: the disclosure fixes the timing (poppet closes before the waist reconnects the concentrate port), which means the upstream land necessarily overlies the concentrate port while the rinse runs. So the opening beneath that port could not be the one shown flowing, and only a station downstream of both lands has a path to the flush bypass. I moved the drawn station and kept the disclosed direction of the jet across the concentrate port, rather than touching the timing, which is inventor text.

I moved the same opening in FIG. 2 as well. The reviewer did not raise it, but leaving FIG. 2 with that opening beneath the concentrate port would have put one physical opening at two different axial stations in two sections of the same valve, which is the same class of defect the review had just found.

In place of citation, the Background states the technical problems in the inventor's own terms: dosing devices whose separation of concentrate from carrier line depends on separately actuated shut-off elements being commanded in the right order and so can be defeated by a control fault, a lost signal or a slow element; residue left on the concentrate port and the check seat that drips between doses and dries or reacts, remedied by breaking the valve out of the line or by a rinse that is a separate commanded operation; and dose settings held by a screw or an electronic value, which are lost during cleaning or need power, a sensor and a display at the valve. input.summary: The only failing mechanical check was brief length: FIG. 3 measured 2906 characters and FIG. 4 measured 2886, against a maximum of 2800. I shortened both briefs by removing invented rendering constraints and redundant phrasing, leaving every disclosed body, opening, contact, flow path and numeral target intact. FIG. 3 keeps the housing and sleeve bands, the annular rinse channel open at both ends, the flush bypass with its conical seat, the poppet head standing clear of that seat with its stem running past the sleeve's left end to the pin, the two-land piston with its shaft and upward pin, the flexible lip, the concentrate port covered by the left land, both radial rinse openings with the left one clear of the piston and aimed toward the concentrate port, and the covered unnumbered opening at the right land. FIG. 4 keeps the collar surrounding the tube with the collar extending leftward past the tube's left end, the helical groove band, the piston rod and follower pin engaged in that band, the three stepped end faces, the three detent recesses, the ball and coil spring, and the three schematic patches carrying no drawing text. What went is padding: sheet-edge phrasing beyond the drawing-area statement, "at the top and bottom" for the housing bands, a duplicated description of the housing interior that leads to the outlet, "a visible gap between them" where the head is already said to stand clear of its seat, the prescription of straight upper and lower collar outlines, and the invented vertical placement of the two hidden detent recesses. Two leader targets were also broadened rather than trimmed only for length: numeral 28 now names a broad interior of the piston instead of an outside-the-outline leader endpoint, and numeral 46 reads "the middle one of the three stepped end faces". No claim, description, numeral definition, drawing description or disclosed embodiment changed, and the per-sheet numeral lists are identical to before.
reasoning: The gate reported a single class of defect, brief length, so I confined the work to figures/FIG-3.md and figures/FIG-4.md and left the application text, the numeral table and draft/07 untouched. FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 were not flagged and were not edited.

I cut from the two categories the drafting rules already treat as removable: generic linework controls and placement constraints with no source in the disclosure. The collar's 'straight upper and lower outlines' is a renderer instruction, not invention geometry, and the vertical positions given for the two broken-line detent recesses ('one part way down and one near the lower outline') were invented to control the render. Neither carries any disclosed relationship.

Where a relationship was stated twice I kept one statement. The flush bypass bullet no longer repeats 'the housing interior that leads to the outlet' because the preceding bullet already establishes it, and the poppet head no longer both 'stands clear to the left of the seat' and has 'a visible gap between them'; the open condition is still expressly drawn.

Target 28 was the largest single saving and also the better target under the endpoint rule: a leader ending outside the outline with a specified arrowhead is an aesthetic coordinate, while a broad interior of the left enlarged portion identifies the piston unambiguously, since neither sealing land carries a numeral on this sheet.
Target 46 was reworded to 'the middle one of the three stepped end faces' so the position is read as a stable middle rather than as an ordinal whose counting direction could go either way.

I preserved the two fixes made for the earlier review, because they resolve findings the gate has already accepted: the collar in FIG. 4 still extends leftward beyond the tube's left end with the tube's hidden outline in broken line, keeping follower pin 44 at one axial station across FIG. 3 and FIG. 4, and the left rinse opening 62 in FIG. 3 still lies clear of both piston portions so its jet has an open path to the flush bypass.

Measured after the edit, FIG. 3 is 2781 bytes and FIG. 4 is 2773 bytes as whole files, and about 2705 and 2697 once the trailing numeral list is discounted, so both clear 2800 under either reading of the check.

figures/FIG-3.md: target 58 shortened to the conical head clear of its seat

figures/FIG-4.md: shortened from 2886 to 2773 characters by removing sheet-edge phrasing, the prescribed straight upper and lower collar outlines, and the invented vertical placement of the two broken-line detent recesses

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is nothing to cite and nothing may be invented; the Background carries no citations and none were added this turn. The brief records that no prior-art search was run, so the art behind this draft may be incomplete and the independent claims should be re-tested against any later search. The claims were not touched. Claim 1 continues to rest on two features that the specification explains in the same words: the axial ordering of the land faces and port edges, which closes the concentrate port before the downstream land uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port so that separation is a property of the moving geometry rather than of command sequencing; and the flush poppet opened by the follower pin carried by the piston rod during the return stroke and closed again before the waist reconnects the concentrate port, so that the rinse cannot be omitted, mistimed or deferred. The index collar with its helical groove, three stop faces, detent and window, the flexible lip, the two directed rinse openings, and the cartridge with threaded end cap remain the graduated fallbacks in claims 2, 3 and 6 to 12 and in the corresponding method claims.
input.answer: The filing gate's single failure, over-length drawing briefs, is fixed. FIG. 3 went from 2906 to 2781 characters and FIG. 4 from 2886 to 2773, both clear of the 2800 maximum. The reductions came from invented rendering constraints and duplicated phrasing, not from invention content: the sheet-edge clauses were reduced to the drawing-area statement, the housing bands no longer carry "at the top and bottom", the flush bypass bullet no longer repeats the description of the housing interior leading to the outlet, the poppet head no longer states both that it stands clear of its seat and that a gap is visible, the collar's prescribed straight upper and lower outlines are gone, and the invented vertical placement of the two broken-line detent recesses is gone. Two leader targets were broadened in the process: numeral 28 now points well inside the hatching of the left enlarged portion of the piston instead of ending outside the outline, and numeral 46 reads "the middle one of the three stepped end faces at the right end". Every disclosed body, opening, contact and flow path in both sheets is preserved, including the collar extending leftward past the tube's left end and the left rinse opening clear of both piston portions. The claims, detailed description, drawing descriptions, numeral table, FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 are unchanged, and the per-sheet numeral lists still match draft/07, draft/08 and draft/numerals.md exactly.

74	Fix every listed item before returning. If an advisory is a false positive, make

Verbalizing a second, permanently open path around the sleeve to the outlet is a substantive flow-path assertion (it would let carrier liquid bypass the sleeve continuously, independently of the flush poppet) and it is untraced. This is not a depiction convention: it is a flow boundary, not an outline.

The briefs verbalize a seat taper ("widening downward into a conical seat") and a contact topology ("a ball resting on the seat"), plus the seat's opening direction into the dose chamber. Taper and contact topology on a functional seat are substantive under this preflight even where the brief says "shown schematically"; only a minimally specific generic element could remain.

In figures/FIG-3.md replace "the right lies at a ball on a conical seat, shown schematically in a passage rising through the upper band" with "the right lies at the one-way outlet valve, shown schematically as a plain closure element in a passage leading up through the upper band."

The source discloses only that a normally closed flush poppet is connected to the flush bypass and is opened by the follower pin near the end of the return stroke. Taper and contact topology on a functional seat, and the routing of a member through a disclosed flow path, are substantive assertions, not depiction conventions.
  - Suggested fix: Replace the bullet with: "Toward the right a passage leads from the bore up through the upper sleeve band toward the outlet: the flush bypass. A plain closure element stands clear of the mouth of that passage and is connected by a plain stem to the follower pin; closure element and stem are shown schematically, without seat, taper or contact detail, and are the flush poppet." Change Target 58 to: "the plain closure element standing clear of the passage mouth." Delete "with a conical seat at the turn" and "along the gap above the sleeve and past the sleeve's left end".

A cam groove is expressly a functional feature for which runout direction is substantive even when the brief calls the geometry schematic; the hand of the helix determines the sense in which each stroke indexes the collar. The source discloses the groove and the fact of one-increment-per-stroke indexing, but not its direction.
  - Suggested fix: Replace with: "A helical cam groove is drawn on the visible cylindrical surface as a narrow band that wraps around the body, shown schematically; its hand and pitch are not indicated."
- **[critical] Axial stop faces verbalized as a monotonic rightward step progression on the collar's end face** (figures/FIG-4.md (Geometry, fourth bullet; Targets, 46)) - The source supports three selectable axial stop faces at differing axial positions that limit piston travel to set three dose volumes. The brief adds an ordered arrangement - three steps of increasing projection in one direction - and locates them on the collar's right end face. The ordering of a set of functional stop faces (which face stands proudest, and in what sequence they are met as the collar indexes) is substantive axial-position information about a functional face, not a generic outline.

The brief adds the opening's axial position relative to both sealing lands and its aim angle. Both are substantive: they define where rinse liquid enters relative to the metering element and in what direction it issues. The added placement is also internally incoherent, because the same brief shows the concentrate port covered by the left (upstream) land, so the verbalized jet from a point downstream of the right land toward that port would pass through the piston body.

An unnumbered ring surrounds the sleeve in the annulus, extending from near the left end of the sleeve rightward to beneath the panel, where a small plain patch shows." In the following description, the terms upstream and downstream refer to the direction of travel of the carrier liquid from the inlet toward the outlet, and the terms axial and radial refer to the axis along which the piston slides.

FIG. 1 shows an inline liquid metering valve 10 having a cylindrical housing 12 with an inlet 14 at one axial end and an outlet 16 at the opposite axial end, a metering sleeve 18 fixed within the housing 12, a cartridge 64 retained in the housing 12 by a threaded end cap 66, and a transparent window 52 in the housing 12.

The inline liquid metering valve 10 is connected in a line that already carries a flowing carrier liquid. Carrier liquid enters at the inlet 14, passes along the housing 12, and leaves at the outlet 16. That flow is the main flow into which each dose of concentrate is delivered, and it is also the flow that rinses the valve. The metering sleeve 18 is spaced radially inward from the inner surface of the housing 12 over part of its length.

FIG. 2 shows the metering sleeve 18 defining a dose chamber 20, a concentrate port 22 opening into the dose chamber 20 and a carrier-liquid admission port 24 opening into the dose chamber 20. FIG. 2 further shows an upstream sealing land 30 and a downstream sealing land 32 joined by a reduced-diameter waist 34 in the fill position, and a one-way outlet valve 38.

The dose chamber 20 is cylindrical. The concentrate port 22 is a radial port through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and is connected in use to a concentrate source. The carrier-liquid admission port 24 passes through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 at an axial position downstream of the concentrate port 22, and admits carrier liquid to the dose chamber 20. The metering sleeve 18 further defines a flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20.

A piston 28 is axially slidable in the dose chamber 20 between a fill position and a discharge position. The upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 are axially spaced from one another on the piston 28 and are joined by the reduced-diameter waist 34. Each sealing land bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20, while the waist 34 stands clear of that wall. A piston rod 36 extends from the piston 28 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 and is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke. The one-way outlet valve 38 is arranged to pass liquid from the dose chamber 20 toward the outlet 16 and to prevent flow in the opposite direction.

In the fill position the waist 34 connects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20, and the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolate the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. Concentrate accordingly passes from the concentrate source through the concentrate port 22 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume of concentrate, the extent of which is fixed by the travel then permitted to the piston 28. Throughout the fill position the carrier-liquid path is closed to the concentrate, because the downstream sealing land 32 overlies the carrier-liquid admission port 24 while the upstream sealing land 30 closes the dose chamber 20 on the other side of the waist 34.

Movement of the piston 28 toward the discharge position closes the concentrate port 22 before the downstream sealing land 32 uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port 24. The upstream sealing land 30 arrives at the concentrate port 22 and shuts it while the downstream sealing land 32 is still overlying the carrier-liquid admission port 24. Only after that has happened does continued travel of the piston 28 carry the downstream sealing land 32 clear of the carrier-liquid admission port 24. Carrier liquid then enters through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume of concentrate in the dose chamber 20 and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16, where it joins the main flow.

The axial ordering of the faces of the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 relative to the edges of the concentrate port 22 and the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is chosen so that the concentrate port 22 is closed at every position of the piston 28 at which the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is open. There is accordingly no position of the piston 28 at which the concentrate source communicates directly with the carrier-liquid path. The separation of the two liquids is a property of the geometry of the piston 28 and the metering sleeve 18. It does not depend on the order in which external commands are given, on any control signal, or on the correct operation of a separately actuated shut-off element. A slow stroke, an interrupted stroke, or a stroke reversed part way through cannot open both ports at once, because the port that must close does so at an earlier point on the same continuous path of travel than the point at which the other port opens.

FIG. 3 shows the piston 28 during the return stroke toward the fill position, with a flexible lip 56, a follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36 and holding a flush poppet 58 open, an annular rinse channel 60, two radial rinse openings 62 of which one is directed across the concentrate port 22, and the flush bypass 26.

The flexible lip 56 is carried on the upstream sealing land 30 and bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20. As the return stroke begins, the flexible lip 56 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20.

The annular rinse channel 60 lies between an outer surface of the metering sleeve 18 and an inner surface of the housing 12, and is supplied with carrier liquid from the inlet 14. The two radial rinse openings 62 pass through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and connect the annular rinse channel 60 to the dose chamber 20. One of the two radial rinse openings 62 is directed across the concentrate port 22 and the other is directed across the one-way outlet valve 38.

The flush poppet 58 is normally closed and is connected to the flush bypass 26. Near the end of the return stroke, the follower pin 44 reaches the flush poppet 58 and opens it. Carrier liquid then flows from the inlet 14 through the annular rinse channel 60, through the two radial rinse openings 62 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 to the outlet 16. The rinse liquid therefore reaches the outlet 16, as the dose does, and is carried away in the main flow.

The flush poppet 58 closes before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. The concentrate port 22 is closed throughout the interval in which the annular rinse channel 60 communicates with the flush bypass 26. Only when the flush poppet 58 has closed does the continuing return of the piston 28 bring the waist 34 back into register with the concentrate port 22, at which point the dose chamber 20 is charged again for the next dose.

Because the follower pin 44 that opens the flush poppet 58 is carried by the piston rod 36, the rinse occurs once for every dose and at the same point in every cycle. It is not a separate operation, it needs no command, and it cannot be omitted while the valve continues to be used. The rinse also occurs while the concentrate port 22 is shut and after the wall of the dose chamber 20 has been wiped.

FIG. 4 shows an index collar 40 having a helical cam groove 42 engaged by the follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36, three selectable axial stop faces 46, a spring-biased detent 48 engaging one of three detent recesses 50, and three dose setting numerals 54.

The index collar 40 surrounds the metering sleeve 18. Each full stroke of the piston 28 draws the follower pin 44 along the helical cam groove 42 and turns the index collar 40 by one increment, so that the index collar 40 advances by itself as the valve is used and needs no separate indexing drive.

The three axial stop faces 46 are carried by the index collar 40 at different axial positions. The stop face presented by the current increment of rotation limits the travel of the piston 28 and thereby sets the dose volume, so that the three axial stop faces 46 correspond to three dose volumes. The spring-biased detent 48 engages one of the three detent recesses 50 to retain the selected setting until the index collar 40 is next indexed.

The transparent window 52 in the housing 12 shows one of the three dose setting numerals 54 carried by the index collar 40. The dose setting numeral presented at the transparent window 52 is the one associated with the axial stop face then limiting the travel of the piston 28, so that the dose setting is mechanically visible without electronics. What is seen at the transparent window 52 is the position of the index collar 40 itself.

The cartridge 64 contains the piston 28, the metering sleeve 18, the one-way outlet valve 38 and the flush poppet 58, and is removable from the housing 12 as a unit. Removing the threaded end cap 66 withdraws the cartridge 64 from the housing 12 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 without disturbing the connections at the inlet 14 and the outlet 16, so that the cartridge 64 is replaced as a unit while the housing 12 remains in the line.

In use, carrier liquid flows through the housing 12 from the inlet 14 to the outlet 16. With the piston 28 in the fill position, concentrate is admitted through the concentrate port 22 and past the waist 34 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume, the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolating the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. The piston 28 is then advanced toward the discharge position so as to close the concentrate port 22 and thereafter to uncover the carrier-liquid admission port 24 with the downstream sealing land 32. Carrier liquid is admitted through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16. The extent of the travel available to the piston 28, and therefore the measured volume, is fixed by the selected one of the three axial stop faces 46.

The piston 28 is then returned toward the fill position. During the return, the flexible lip 56 on the upstream sealing land 30 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20, and the follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36 opens the normally closed flush poppet 58. Carrier liquid flows through the annular rinse channel 60 between the metering sleeve 18 and the housing 12, through the two radial rinse openings 62 in the metering sleeve 18 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20 to the outlet 16. The flush poppet 58 is closed before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. Over the same full stroke, the follower pin 44 travelling in the helical cam groove 42 turns the index collar 40 by one increment, the spring-biased detent 48 enters the next of the three detent recesses 50, and the dose setting numeral then presented at the transparent window 52 shows the setting that will govern the next dose. The valve is thereby left charged, rinsed and set, ready for the following cycle.

The foregoing description sets out embodiments of the invention. A skilled reader may make changes of detail to the described embodiments without departing from the scope of the claims that follow.

# FIG. 1

View: longitudinal sectional view of the inline liquid metering valve, axis horizontal. All line work lies well inside the drawing area.

Geometry:

- The housing is an elongate cylinder cut lengthwise on its axis, appearing as upper and lower hatched wall bands that run across most of the view, joined at the right by a hatched end wall. The interior between them is open.
- The left end of the housing is closed by a threaded end cap, a short hatched ring seated in the left mouth, meeting the housing bore along a shallow saw-tooth interface indicating a thread. A plain shaft on the axis extends leftward from the body, out of the left end of the sleeve bore, and is broken off at a conventional break line short of the end cap.
- A short tubular stub projects axially leftward from the left end of the housing below the axis, clear of the end cap and the shaft, and opens into the interior; it is the inlet, shown schematically. A second such stub projects axially rightward from the end wall at the right and opens into the interior; it is the outlet, shown schematically. Both stubs end well inside the drawing area.
- The metering sleeve lies inside the housing on the same axis, drawn as an upper hatched band and a lower hatched band spaced inward from the housing wall bands, so that a clear gap is visible above and below it over the portion of its length right of the ring described below.
- The sleeve, the body in its bore and the parts they carry are drawn as one removable unit, the sleeve's left end standing within the left mouth of the housing short of the end cap; this unit is the cartridge.
- Within the sleeve bore, in the left half, is a body shown schematically as two hatched enlarged portions joined by a narrower middle portion, with the plain shaft running leftward from it.
- An unnumbered ring surrounds the sleeve in the annulus over the left portion of its length, its left part standing beyond the sleeve's left end, clear of that gap.
- A rectangular unhatched panel is set into the upper housing wall band above the ring, the hatching stopping at its outline; it is the transparent window. On the ring beneath the panel a small plain patch shows.

Numerals on this sheet: 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 52, 64, 66.

Targets:

- 10: the hatched upper housing wall band.

View: enlarged longitudinal section of the metering portion of FIG. 1 during the return stroke, axis horizontal, with the flush poppet held open. All line work lies well inside the drawing area.

Geometry:

- An outer housing wall appears in section as upper and lower hatched bands. Inside it the sleeve wall appears as upper and lower hatched bands spaced inward; between them is the bore.

content.content:
17	The axial ordering of the faces of the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 relative to the edges of the concentrate port 22 and the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is chosen so that the concentrate port 22 is closed at every position of the piston 28 at which the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is open. There is accordingly no position of the piston 28 at which the concentrate source communicates directly with the carrier-liquid path. The separation of the two liquids is a property of the geometry of the piston 28 and the metering sleeve 18. It does not depend on the order in which external commands are given, on any control signal, or on the correct operation of a separately actuated shut-off element. A slow stroke, an interrupted stroke, or a stroke reversed part way through cannot open both ports at once, because the port that must close does so at an earlier point on the same continuous path of travel than the point at which the other port opens.
18	
19	FIG. 3 shows the piston 28 during the return stroke toward the fill position, with a flexible lip 56, a follower pin 44 holding a flush poppet 58 open, an annular rinse channel 60, two radial rinse openings 62 of which one is directed across the concentrate port 22, and the flush bypass 26. The follower pin 44 is carried by the piston rod 36.
20	
21	The flexible lip 56 is carried on the upstream sealing land 30 and bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20. As the return stroke begins, the flexible lip 56 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20.
22	
23	The annular rinse channel 60 lies between an outer surface of the metering sleeve 18 and an inner surface of the housing 12, and is supplied with carrier liquid from the inlet 14. The two radial rinse openings 62 pass through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and connect the annular rinse channel 60 to the dose chamber 20. One of the two radial rinse openings 62 is directed across the concentrate port 22 and the other is directed across the one-way outlet valve 38.
24	
25	The flush poppet 58 is normally closed and is connected to the flush bypass 26. Near the end of the return stroke, the follower pin 44 reaches the flush poppet 58 and opens it. Carrier liquid then flows from the inlet 14 through the annular rinse channel 60, through the two radial rinse openings 62 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 to the outlet 16. The rinse liquid therefore reaches the outlet 16, as the dose does, and is carried away in the main flow.
26	
27	The flush poppet 58 closes before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. The concentrate port 22 is closed throughout the interval in which the annular rinse channel 60 communicates with the flush bypass 26. Only when the flush poppet 58 has closed does the continuing return of the piston 28 bring the waist 34 back into register with the concentrate port 22, at which point the dose chamber 20 is charged again for the next dose.
28	
29	Because the follower pin 44 that opens the flush poppet 58 is carried by the piston rod 36, the rinse occurs once for every dose and at the same point in every cycle. It is not a separate operation, it needs no command, and it cannot be omitted while the valve continues to be used. The rinse also occurs while the concentrate port 22 is shut and after the wall of the dose chamber 20 has been wiped.

The axial ordering of the faces of the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 relative to the edges of the concentrate port 22 and the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is chosen so that the concentrate port 22 is closed at every position of the piston 28 at which the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is open. There is accordingly no position of the piston 28 at which the concentrate source communicates directly with the carrier-liquid path. The separation of the two liquids is a property of the geometry of the piston 28 and the metering sleeve 18. It does not depend on the order in which external commands are given, on any control signal, or on the correct operation of a separately actuated shut-off element. A slow stroke, an interrupted stroke, or a stroke reversed part way through cannot open both ports at once, because the port that must close does so at an earlier point on the same continuous path of travel than the point at which the other port opens.

FIG. 3 shows the piston 28 during the return stroke toward the fill position, with a flexible lip 56, a follower pin 44 holding a flush poppet 58 open, an annular rinse channel 60, two radial rinse openings 62 of which one is directed across the concentrate port 22, and the flush bypass 26. The follower pin 44 is carried by the piston rod 36.

The flexible lip 56 is carried on the upstream sealing land 30 and bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20. As the return stroke begins, the flexible lip 56 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20.

The annular rinse channel 60 lies between an outer surface of the metering sleeve 18 and an inner surface of the housing 12, and is supplied with carrier liquid from the inlet 14. The two radial rinse openings 62 pass through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and connect the annular rinse channel 60 to the dose chamber 20. One of the two radial rinse openings 62 is directed across the concentrate port 22 and the other is directed across the one-way outlet valve 38.

The flush poppet 58 is normally closed and is connected to the flush bypass 26. Near the end of the return stroke, the follower pin 44 reaches the flush poppet 58 and opens it. Carrier liquid then flows from the inlet 14 through the annular rinse channel 60, through the two radial rinse openings 62 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 to the outlet 16. The rinse liquid therefore reaches the outlet 16, as the dose does, and is carried away in the main flow.

The flush poppet 58 closes before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. The concentrate port 22 is closed throughout the interval in which the annular rinse channel 60 communicates with the flush bypass 26. Only when the flush poppet 58 has closed does the continuing return of the piston 28 bring the waist 34 back into register with the concentrate port 22, at which point the dose chamber 20 is charged again for the next dose.

Because the follower pin 44 that opens the flush poppet 58 is carried by the piston rod 36, the rinse occurs once for every dose and at the same point in every cycle. It is not a separate operation, it needs no command, and it cannot be omitted while the valve continues to be used. The rinse also occurs while the concentrate port 22 is shut and after the wall of the dose chamber 20 has been wiped.

content.text: All findings are addressed and every brief is now under the length cap (FIG. 1: 2714, FIG. 2: 2793, FIG. 3: 2786, FIG. 4: 2727 characters).

input.summary: Every listed item is fixed, and all of the substantive fixes are deletions or genericising rewrites inside figures/; no claim, description sentence, numeral definition or embodiment was widened to accommodate a drawing. The seven critical items: the annular rinse channel no longer has open ends into the housing interior in FIG. 1 or FIG. 3, leaving the single disclosed flush route of channel, rinse openings, flush bypass, outlet; the one-way outlet valve is now a plain closure element across a passage in FIG. 2 and FIG. 3, with no seat taper or contact topology, and target 38 follows; the flush poppet is a plain closure element standing clear of the passage mouth and joined by a plain stem to the follower pin, with the conical head, conical seat, seat location and the stem route through the rinse channel all deleted; the cam groove is a narrow band wrapping the body with hand and pitch not indicated; the stop faces are three faces at three axial positions on one stepped end face, with the ordering not indicated and target 46 reading "one of the three stepped end faces"; the numbered rinse opening no longer carries an axial position relative to the lands or an aim angle, so the incoherent blocked jet is gone; and the flexible lip is a thin flexible projection contacting each bore wall, with flare direction not indicated. The two major items: FIG. 1 now puts the unnumbered ring in the left length of the annulus with its left part beyond the sleeve's left end, where FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 put the follower pin, limits the clear gap to the length of the annulus right of that ring, and sets the transparent window above the ring so the window still shows a numeral carried on the collar; and the piston rod is broken off at a conventional break line short of the end cap, asserting neither a blind end nor a cap penetration. The four minor items: the concentrate connection is a short stub broken off within the view in both FIG. 2 and FIG. 3; the detent is a plain detent element seated in a plain recess with a spring behind it shown broken off, with targets 48 and 50 following; numerals.md rows 46, 50, 54 and 62 are singular; and claim 9 now recites "one of the three dose setting numerals" associated with "a selected one of the three selectable axial stop faces", curing both singular terms. On numeral 36 and FIG. 3: the sheet already carries the maximum of eight numerals, so instead of a ninth the description's FIG. 3 recitation no longer states that the piston rod 36 is shown there, and a following sentence states that the follower pin 44 is carried by the piston rod 36; the pin keeps its indefinite first mention and the rod stays labelled on FIG. 4. All four briefs were also trimmed back under the 2800 character cap that the previous gate enforced.
reasoning: Every critical item was an assertion about a functional surface that the disclosure does not describe, so each was cured by deleting the assertion and leaving the least specific outline that still shows the disclosed function: a plain closure element for both the one-way outlet valve and the flush poppet, a plain recess and a plain detent element, a groove band without hand, and a lip without flare direction. Nothing about the invention was narrowed, because none of these forms ever appeared in the claims, the summary or the detailed description.

The rinse channel fix mattered most for the invention rather than for the drawing: an annulus open at both ends into the housing interior would have depicted a permanent bypass around the sleeve, which would undercut the very feature claim 1 rests on, namely that carrier liquid reaches the outlet through the flush bypass only when the follower pin holds the poppet open. Removing the open ends restores the single ordered path the disclosure gives.

For the collar, the constraint was that the disclosure puts both the index collar and the annular rinse channel between the sleeve and the housing, while the follower pin must reach the groove from the piston rod. I put the ring in the left length of the annulus, where FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 already place the pin, and limited the rinse gap to the length right of it. The window moved to sit above the ring rather than midway, because the window must show a numeral carried on the collar; keeping it midway would have separated it from the collar it reads.

The piston rod break line was chosen over either alternative on purpose. The source says nothing about how the rod is driven or whether it leaves the housing, so a blind end contradicts the description's driven stroke while a cap penetration would invent a seal and a drive path. A conventional break line asserts neither and is silent in the way the source is silent.

On numeral 36, the reviewer's suggested cure would have made nine numerals on FIG. 3, one over the per sheet maximum, and every numeral on that sheet is needed there: 26, 56, 58, 60 and 62 appear nowhere else, 28 is the piston as a whole, and 22 anchors the rinse opening that is directed across it. So I removed the assertion instead of adding the label, by taking 36 out of the FIG. 3 recitation sentence and stating the rod relationship in a following sentence of body text. The pin still gets its indefinite first mention in the FIG. 3 paragraph, which is what the earlier antecedent fix required.

Claim 9 was redrafted rather than patched with an article, because both singular terms lacked antecedents and claim 7 supplies the plural set: the window now shows one of the three dose setting numerals, and that one is tied to a selected one of the three selectable axial stop faces. The detailed description already says exactly this, so no support was added.

The singular numeral table entries were taken because each leader lands on one member of a group. The description still reads three axial stop faces 46, three detent recesses 50, three dose setting numerals 54 and two radial rinse openings 62, which remains correct with a singular part name in the table and keeps one meaning per numeral.

Length had to be managed while making these edits, since the previous gate rejected FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 for exceeding 2800 characters and the genericising rewrites added words. I recovered the space from invented rendering constraints rather than from geometry: sheet-edge clauses beyond the drawing-area statement, a restated explanation of a break line, and over-specified leader endpoints such as the FIG. 1 numeral 10 leader ending just outside the housing outline, which is now a broad interior target on the upper housing wall band.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the Background carries no citations and none may be invented; the brief records that no prior-art search was run, so the art behind this draft may be incomplete and the independent claims should be re-tested against any later search. Nothing in this turn touched the shape of the claimed combination. Claim 1 still rests on the axial ordering of the land faces and port edges, which closes the concentrate port before the downstream land uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port so that separation is enforced by the moving geometry rather than by command sequencing, and on the flush poppet opened by the follower pin carried by the piston rod during the return stroke and closed again before the waist reconnects the concentrate port. The Background states the problems those two features answer, including shut-off elements that depend on being commanded in the right order and rinses that are separate commanded operations, which is the material a later argument would be built from. Removing the invented seat tapers, ball contacts, helix hand and stop-face ordering from the figure briefs also keeps the disclosure from reading onto conventional check-valve and detent vocabulary for a different thing, since those forms were never part of the claimed combination.
input.answer: All fourteen listed items are fixed. The seven critical ones were cured inside the figure briefs by deleting untraced functional-surface geometry: the rinse channel's open ends into the housing interior are gone from FIG. 1 and FIG. 3, leaving the disclosed route of channel, rinse openings, flush bypass, outlet; the one-way outlet valve and the flush poppet are now plain closure elements without seat taper, contact topology or stem routing, with targets 38 and 58 following; the cam groove's hand and pitch are not indicated; the stop faces sit on one stepped end face with their order not indicated and target 46 reading "one of the three stepped end faces"; the numbered rinse opening carries no position relative to the lands and no aim angle, which also removes the blocked jet; and the flexible lip has no flare direction. The two major ones: FIG. 1 now places the unnumbered ring in the left length of the annulus with its left part beyond the sleeve's left end, limits the clear gap to the length right of it, and sets the window above the ring, so the collar and the rinse channel occupy different lengths of one annulus and the window still reads the collar; and the piston rod is broken off at a conventional break line, asserting neither a blind end nor a cap penetration. The four minor ones: break-line stubs for the concentrate connection in FIG. 2 and FIG. 3; a plain detent element in a plain recess with a spring shown broken off; singular part names for numerals 46, 50, 54 and 62; and claim 9 rewritten to recite one of the three dose setting numerals associated with a selected one of the three selectable axial stop faces. Numeral 36 could not be added to FIG. 3 without a ninth numeral on a sheet already at the maximum of eight, so the description's FIG. 3 recitation no longer says the rod is shown there and a following sentence states that the follower pin 44 is carried by the piston rod 36; the rod stays labelled on FIG. 4. All four briefs are back under the 2800 character cap.

structured_output.summary: Every listed item is fixed, and all of the substantive fixes are deletions or genericising rewrites inside figures/; no claim, description sentence, numeral definition or embodiment was widened to accommodate a drawing. The seven critical items: the annular rinse channel no longer has open ends into the housing interior in FIG. 1 or FIG. 3, leaving the single disclosed flush route of channel, rinse openings, flush bypass, outlet; the one-way outlet valve is now a plain closure element across a passage in FIG. 2 and FIG. 3, with no seat taper or contact topology, and target 38 follows; the flush poppet is a plain closure element standing clear of the passage mouth and joined by a plain stem to the follower pin, with the conical head, conical seat, seat location and the stem route through the rinse channel all deleted; the cam groove is a narrow band wrapping the body with hand and pitch not indicated; the stop faces are three faces at three axial positions on one stepped end face, with the ordering not indicated and target 46 reading "one of the three stepped end faces"; the numbered rinse opening no longer carries an axial position relative to the lands or an aim angle, so the incoherent blocked jet is gone; and the flexible lip is a thin flexible projection contacting each bore wall, with flare direction not indicated. The two major items: FIG. 1 now puts the unnumbered ring in the left length of the annulus with its left part beyond the sleeve's left end, where FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 put the follower pin, limits the clear gap to the length of the annulus right of that ring, and sets the transparent window above the ring so the window still shows a numeral carried on the collar; and the piston rod is broken off at a conventional break line short of the end cap, asserting neither a blind end nor a cap penetration. The four minor items: the concentrate connection is a short stub broken off within the view in both FIG. 2 and FIG. 3; the detent is a plain detent element seated in a plain recess with a spring behind it shown broken off, with targets 48 and 50 following; numerals.md rows 46, 50, 54 and 62 are singular; and claim 9 now recites "one of the three dose setting numerals" associated with "a selected one of the three selectable axial stop faces", curing both singular terms. On numeral 36 and FIG. 3: the sheet already carries the maximum of eight numerals, so instead of a ninth the description's FIG. 3 recitation no longer states that the piston rod 36 is shown there, and a following sentence states that the follower pin 44 is carried by the piston rod 36; the pin keeps its indefinite first mention and the rod stays labelled on FIG. 4. All four briefs were also trimmed back under the 2800 character cap that the previous gate enforced.
reasoning: Every critical item was an assertion about a functional surface that the disclosure does not describe, so each was cured by deleting the assertion and leaving the least specific outline that still shows the disclosed function: a plain closure element for both the one-way outlet valve and the flush poppet, a plain recess and a plain detent element, a groove band without hand, and a lip without flare direction. Nothing about the invention was narrowed, because none of these forms ever appeared in the claims, the summary or the detailed description.

The rinse channel fix mattered most for the invention rather than for the drawing: an annulus open at both ends into the housing interior would have depicted a permanent bypass around the sleeve, which would undercut the very feature claim 1 rests on, namely that carrier liquid reaches the outlet through the flush bypass only when the follower pin holds the poppet open. Removing the open ends restores the single ordered path the disclosure gives.

For the collar, the constraint was that the disclosure puts both the index collar and the annular rinse channel between the sleeve and the housing, while the follower pin must reach the groove from the piston rod. I put the ring in the left length of the annulus, where FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 already place the pin, and limited the rinse gap to the length right of it. The window moved to sit above the ring rather than midway, because the window must show a numeral carried on the collar; keeping it midway would have separated it from the collar it reads.

The piston rod break line was chosen over either alternative on purpose. The source says nothing about how the rod is driven or whether it leaves the housing, so a blind end contradicts the description's driven stroke while a cap penetration would invent a seal and a drive path. A conventional break line asserts neither and is silent in the way the source is silent.

On numeral 36, the reviewer's suggested cure would have made nine numerals on FIG. 3, one over the per sheet maximum, and every numeral on that sheet is needed there: 26, 56, 58, 60 and 62 appear nowhere else, 28 is the piston as a whole, and 22 anchors the rinse opening that is directed across it. So I removed the assertion instead of adding the label, by taking 36 out of the FIG. 3 recitation sentence and stating the rod relationship in a following sentence of body text. The pin still gets its indefinite first mention in the FIG. 3 paragraph, which is what the earlier antecedent fix required.

Claim 9 was redrafted rather than patched with an article, because both singular terms lacked antecedents and claim 7 supplies the plural set: the window now shows one of the three dose setting numerals, and that one is tied to a selected one of the three selectable axial stop faces. The detailed description already says exactly this, so no support was added.

The singular numeral table entries were taken because each leader lands on one member of a group. The description still reads three axial stop faces 46, three detent recesses 50, three dose setting numerals 54 and two radial rinse openings 62, which remains correct with a singular part name in the table and keeps one meaning per numeral.

Length had to be managed while making these edits, since the previous gate rejected FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 for exceeding 2800 characters and the genericising rewrites added words. I recovered the space from invented rendering constraints rather than from geometry: sheet-edge clauses beyond the drawing-area statement, a restated explanation of a break line, and over-specified leader endpoints such as the FIG. 1 numeral 10 leader ending just outside the housing outline, which is now a broad interior target on the upper housing wall band.

1	# Previous review - verdict: fail
2	
3	Source-fidelity preflight (v10, functional-surface geometry) over input/disclosure.md, input/conversation.md, input/brief.md, draft/01–10, draft/numerals.md and figures/FIG-1..4.md.
4	
5	LEDGER RESULT - application text. Every claim limitation in claims 1–20 traces to an affirmative USER passage. Independent claim 1 (housing/inlet/outlet; metering sleeve defining dose chamber, concentrate port, carrier-liquid admission port, flush bypass opening downstream of the dose chamber; annular rinse channel between sleeve OD and housing ID with at least one rinse opening; piston with upstream/downstream sealing lands joined by a reduced-diameter waist; piston rod carrying a follower pin; one-way outlet valve; normally closed flush poppet; the fill-position isolation; the close-before-uncover ordering; the follower-pin-opened rinse closing before the waist reconnects) maps sentence-for-sentence onto disclosure ¶¶2–4. Dependent claims 2–12 and 15–20 (two radial rinse openings directed across the concentrate port and the one-way outlet valve; flexible lip on the upstream land; concentrate port closed during the rinse interval; axial ordering of land faces and port edges; index collar with helical cam groove turned one increment per full stroke; three axial stop faces; spring-biased detent and three recesses; transparent window and three dose-setting numerals; cartridge and threaded end cap; cylindrical housing with end inlet/outlet) each trace to disclosure ¶¶3–5. Method claims 13–14, 17–19 mirror the same ordered sequence the inventor asked to be claimed ("An apparatus claim and a method claim should cover the ordered isolation, metering, discharge, and automatic rinse sequence"). The renaming of the inventor's "three reference numerals carried on the collar" to "dose setting numerals 54" is a permissible anti-ambiguity term and is used consistently in the summary, description, claims and FIG. 4. All six brief-mandated terms are preserved. Title, cross-reference ("Not applicable."), government support ("Not applicable."), applicant/inventor are per input/brief.md. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced, per instructions. Abstract is a single paragraph under 150 words and adds nothing beyond the source.
6	
7	One untraced description statement was found: "spaced radially inward … over part of its length" (finding 8).
8	
9	LEDGER RESULT - figures. Numerals 10–66 in numerals.md all correspond to disclosed parts, and each figure sheet's numeral list matches the numerals recited for that figure in draft/08. Depiction conventions I accepted rather than reported, because the underlying part is affirmatively disclosed, the brief calls the shape schematic, and the application text stays shape-neutral: the generic tubular inlet/outlet stubs and the radial offset of the inlet stub below the axis in FIG. 1 (forced by the disclosed end cap and rod exit; not verbalized anywhere in the application text); the up/down side allocation of the concentrate port and admission port in a longitudinal section (a section must place each port on one side, and the opposed placement of the rinse openings is affirmatively supported by "directed across the concentrate port and the one-way outlet valve"); the plain seatless closure elements for the one-way outlet valve and flush poppet; the unflared flexible lip ("shown schematically without flare direction"); the collar's stepped end face with the hand/pitch of the cam groove and the angular order of stop faces, recesses and numerals expressly left unindicated; and the blank patches standing for the dose-setting numerals. No "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language leaks into draft/06–08, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question or unresolved alternative remains anywhere in draft/ or figures/.
10	
11	EIGHT FINDINGS, all with concrete fixes:
